chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad, both from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman al-Minqari, from Abd al-Razzaq ibn Hammam, from Ma'mar ibn Rashid, from al-Zuhri Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Ubaydullah, who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was asked, 'Which of the deeds is most superior in the presence of Allah?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no deed, after the recognition of Allah, Exalted and Mighty, and the recognition of His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), that is more superior than hatred of the world. For that [hatred] are many branches, and for the disobediences are branches.'
So the first thing with which Allah was disobeyed was arrogance, the disobedience of Iblis when he refused and was arrogant, and he was of the disbelievers.

Then [comes] greed, and it is the disobedience of Adam and Hawwa (peace be upon them) when Allah, Exalted and Mighty, said to them, 'Eat from wherever you wish, but do not approach this tree, lest you become of the unjust.' So they took what they had no need for, and that entered into their offspring until the Day of Resurrection, and that is that most of what the son of Adam seeks is what he has no need for.

Then [comes] envy, and it is the disobedience of the son of Adam when he envied his brother and killed him. So from that branched out the love of women, and the love of the world, and the love of leadership, and the love of comfort, and the love of speech, and the love of exaltedness and wealth. Thus they became seven traits, and they all gathered in the love of the world.
So the Prophets and the Scholars said after recognizing that: 'The love of the world is the head of every sin, and the world is two worlds: a world of bare necessities and a condemned world.'
ai.seo_question: What is the most superior deed after knowing Allah according to Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes that hatred of the world (bukh' al-dunya) is the supreme deed following divine recognition, tracing spiritual decline from Iblis's arrogance to Adam's greed and Cain's envy. It identifies the love of the world as the root of seven specific vices, culminating in the Prophetic and Scholarly consensus that it is the 'head of all sin,' distinguishing between the world of provision and the accursed world of distraction.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali Bin Muhammad, altogether from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Suleyman Al Minqary, from Abdul Razzaq Bin Hammam, from Moamar Bin Rashid, from Al Zuhry Muhammad Bin Muslim Bin Ubeydullah who said,

‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was asked, ‘Which of the deeds is superior in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no deed, after the recognition of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic and recognition of His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup> more superior than hatred of the world. There are many branches for that, and for the disobedience, there is one branch’.

So the first of what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> was disobeyed with was the arrogance, being a disobedience of Iblees<sup>la</sup>, where he<sup>la</sup> refused (to prostrate) and was arrogant, and he<sup>la</sup> was from the disbelievers’.

Then (it was) the greed, and it is the disobedience of Adamas and Hawwaas [7:19] so eat from wherever you desire, but do not go near this tree, for then you will be of the unjust. So theyas both took what there was no need to it for them both. Thus, that entered into theiras offspring up to the Day of Judgement, and that is that most of what the son of Adamas seeks is what there is no need to it for him.

Then (it was) the envy, and it is a disobedience of the son<sup>la</sup> of Adam<sup>as</sup> where he<sup>la</sup> envied his<sup>la</sup> brother<sup>as</sup>, and he<sup>la</sup> killed him<sup>as</sup>. So there branched out from that, the love of women, and the love of the world, and love of the leadership, and love of the relaxation, and love of the speech, and love of the exaltedness and the wealth. Thus, these came to be seven traits, and they all gathered in the love of the world.

Thus the Prophets<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> and the Scholars<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said after recognition that: ‘The love of the world is the head of all sins, and the world is (two types of) world – a world of bare necessities and the condemned one’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Ali ibn Muhammad all from al- Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman al-Minqari from ‘Abd al-Razzaq ibn Hammam from Mu’ammar ibn Rashid from al-Zuhri Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn ‘Ubayd Allah who has said the following:

“Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) was asked, ‘Which deed is more excellent before Allah?’ The Imam said, ‘No deed, after knowing Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, and knowing the Messenger of Allah, is more excellent than hating the world. It has many branches, and the sins have branches also.
The first sin committed was Arrogance, the sin of Satan, when he refused to obey (Allah), assumed arrogance and became an unbeliever.

Thereafter it is Greed, the sin of Adam and Eve. When Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, told them, ‘Enjoy the foods therein, but do not go near a certain tree lest you become of the transgressors.’ [2:35] They took what they did not need and it remained in their descendents to the Day of Judgment. For this reason most of the things that the children of Adam want do not need them.

Thereafter is Envy. It is the sin of the son of Adam who envied his brother and killed him. From this branches love for women, love for the world, love to become the leader, the love to be comfortable, the love to speak, the love to be superior and rich. They total seven characteristics and all are found in the love for the world.
The prophets and the scholars after knowing this have said, ‘Love for the world is the head of all sins.’ The world is of two kinds: The world of bare necessities and the condemned one.’”
